blocks.text: Docker (2013, from dotCloud) didn't invent kernel isolation. It invented the workflow that made containers a standard developer tool: a buildable, layered, portable image, shared through registries and driven by a simple CLI.

rows: Image as the unit of delivery
App + userland in one immutable artifact
Distribution and sharing, like GitHub for images
Ended most "works on my machine" issues

blocks.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]

items: Isolation still comes from namespaces and cgroups on a shared kernel.
Persistence, secrets and orchestration still needed separate solutions (volumes, secret stores, Compose, Kubernetes).

blocks.text: Q: "What did Docker actually contribute?" A: "Not isolation: namespaces, cgroups and LXC already existed. Docker contributed the packaging and distribution model (layered images, the Dockerfile, registries) plus a developer-friendly CLI, which made one immutable artifact runnable everywhere."

items: Isolation, persistence and orchestration came from elsewhere.
